name: MASTER PROJECT PROMPT: BUILD A WORLD-CLASS

messages.content:
MASTER PROJECT PROMPT: BUILD A WORLD-CLASS LUXURY GHEE BRAND WEBSITE

Act as an elite multidisciplinary digital product team consisting of:

* A world-class luxury ecommerce art director.
* A senior UI/UX designer specializing in premium consumer brands.
* An award-winning brand identity designer.
* A senior frontend engineer.
* A motion designer specializing in subtle, high-end interactions.
* A conversion-rate optimization specialist.
* A mobile-first responsive design engineer.
* A premium food and lifestyle photographer’s creative director.

Your task is to DESIGN AND BUILD a complete, exceptionally polished, premium ecommerce website for a single-product Indian artisanal food brand selling 100% pure, homemade buffalo-milk ghee.

This is not a design exercise where you merely produce a screenshot.

Build a real, working, responsive website with functional navigation, a proper shopping experience, a product purchase flow, realistic product presentation, and exceptionally polished frontend implementation.

The finished result must feel like a website created by a highly experienced professional agency for a premium Indian food company.

It must NOT look like a generic AI-generated website, a basic Shopify template, a student project, or a collection of random design components.

Every visual decision must feel intentional.

Every interaction must serve a purpose.

Every section must contribute to the brand story, product desirability, usability, or conversion.

Prioritize visual quality, craftsmanship, performance, responsiveness, and attention to detail over unnecessary complexity.

Do not rush the implementation.

Do not stop after creating the hero section.

Build the entire experience.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. BRAND FOUNDATION
    ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

BUSINESS CATEGORY:
Premium Indian artisanal ghee.

PRODUCT:
100% pure, homemade ghee made from buffalo milk.

PRODUCT PRICE:
₹1,000 per kilogram.

PRODUCT COUNT:
Exactly ONE main product.

BRAND POSITIONING:
A premium, authentic, Indian household staple presented with the sophistication of a luxury artisanal food brand.

The brand should communicate purity, craftsmanship, warmth, tradition, quality, and quiet luxury.

It should feel premium without being pretentious.

It should feel traditional without looking outdated.

It should feel modern without losing its Indian identity.

It should communicate quality through thoughtful presentation, beautiful photography, elegant typography, and confident copywriting rather than exaggerated marketing claims.

IMPORTANT:
If a brand name has not been provided, use “AAVRIT” as a temporary working brand name.

Keep the brand name centralized in the code so it can be replaced easily later.

Do not create multiple unrelated products.

Do not create fake product variants.

Do not invent a founder, farm location, family history, certification, awards, laboratory results, customer testimonials, customer counts, or years of experience.

Do not claim organic certification, grass-fed sourcing, traditional bilona preparation, chemical-free production, medicinal benefits, or any other attribute unless explicitly verified by the owner.

The website must distinguish between known product information and details that the business owner still needs to provide.

The price must be displayed clearly and consistently:

₹1,000 / kg

The product is buffalo-milk ghee, not cow ghee.

Never accidentally describe it as cow ghee.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
02. CREATIVE DIRECTION: QUIET ROYAL LUXURY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The website must look expensive because of its composition, materials, typography, photography, spacing, and restraint.

Do not make it look expensive by adding gold gradients to everything.

The visual identity should be inspired by a sophisticated combination of:

* Luxury Indian heritage brands.
* Premium editorial magazines.
* Boutique gourmet food companies.
* Contemporary artisanal packaging.
* High-end lifestyle photography.
* Refined modern ecommerce.

The aesthetic should feel like a carefully art-directed luxury product campaign.

Use generous whitespace.

Use carefully controlled asymmetry.

Use strong editorial compositions.

Use subtle borders.

Use restrained metallic accents.

Use large, beautifully typeset headings.

Use rich photographic textures.

Use a deliberate visual hierarchy.

Use consistent spacing throughout.

The site must have a recognizable identity even if all branding elements are temporarily hidden.

PRIMARY COLOR PALETTE

Use the following colors as the foundation of the design.

Deep Forest Green:
#173C2E

Use this as the primary brand color for selected backgrounds, navigation accents, important buttons, and branded sections.

Dark Heritage Green:
#10291F

Use this for deeper sections, footer backgrounds, and occasional dramatic contrast.

Antique Gold:
#B39458

Use this sparingly for fine borders, tiny decorative details, selected icons, and subtle accents.

Warm Ivory:
#F7F3E9

Use this as the main page background.

Soft Cream:
#EFE6D4

Use this for alternate sections, product information panels, and subtle surface variation.

Rich Ghee Gold:
#D8A33E

Use this for photographic color direction and occasional product accents. Avoid using it as a dominant UI color.

Deep Charcoal:
#24251F

Use for primary body text and headings where a light background is used.

Muted Olive:
#777B64

Use for secondary information, subtle labels, and supporting text.

White:
#FFFFFF

Use selectively for product surfaces, cards, and clean contrasts.

COLOR DISTRIBUTION

The website should predominantly use warm ivory and cream.

Deep green should create moments of richness and contrast.

Gold should function as a restrained accent rather than a decorative obsession.

Never use bright yellow as the main background.

Never use shiny gold gradients across entire sections.

Never use excessive beige cards stacked on top of beige sections.

Never use random purple, blue, pink, or neon accents.

Never use a different color palette for every section.

The entire website must feel like one coherent brand.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
03. TYPOGRAPHY SYSTEM
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Typography is one of the most important aspects of the project.

Choose a sophisticated editorial serif for major headings and a clean, highly legible sans-serif for body text and interface elements.

Suggested combination:

HEADINGS:
Cormorant Garamond or an equally refined editorial serif.

BODY AND UI:
Manrope or a similarly polished modern sans-serif.

Use a reliable font-loading strategy with sensible fallback fonts.

Do not use too many font families.

Use no more than two primary font families unless a third is essential for a specific brand element.

TYPOGRAPHIC HIERARCHY

Hero heading:
Large, elegant, editorial, and confidently composed.

Desktop target:
Approximately 64–88px, adjusted to the actual composition.

Mobile target:
Approximately 42–56px, with responsive scaling.

Section headings:
Approximately 38–54px on desktop and 30–40px on mobile.

Product name:
Large enough to feel important without overwhelming the product photography.

Body copy:
Approximately 15–18px with comfortable line height.

Small labels:
Approximately 10–12px, using carefully controlled letter spacing.

Price:
Prominent, readable, and visually connected to the purchase action.

Use fluid typography where appropriate.

Headings must wrap naturally.

Never allow a heading to collide with an image, overflow the viewport, or become awkwardly narrow.

Use uppercase lettering selectively for small editorial labels.

Do not turn every sentence into uppercase text.

Do not use excessive letter spacing on normal body text.

The final typography should feel carefully typeset by a designer rather than automatically generated.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
04. ART DIRECTION AND PRODUCT PHOTOGRAPHY
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Photography will determine whether this website looks genuinely premium.

Use high-quality, realistic food photography with a carefully controlled visual style.

The hero image should be the strongest visual asset on the website.

HERO IMAGE CONCEPT

Create a sophisticated product composition featuring:

* A beautifully crafted jar of golden buffalo-milk ghee.
* A rich, naturally textured ghee surface.
* A small traditional brass spoon or restrained brass serving element.
* Warm directional sunlight.
* Soft natural shadows.
* A warm ivory, earthy, or dark forest-green setting.
* A subtle Indian artisanal atmosphere.
* Realistic reflections and believable material textures.
* A carefully composed editorial arrangement.

The ghee must look appetizing and physically realistic.

Its golden color must feel natural rather than artificially neon-yellow.

The container should have believable proportions and realistic glass, ceramic, or food-grade packaging characteristics.

Do not add fake certifications or illegible AI-generated labels to the jar.

If the brand label is rendered in the photograph, keep it simple and ensure the actual brand name is spelled correctly.

Prefer a genuine, high-quality product photograph or a deliberately art-directed image asset over a collection of generic stock photographs.

If image generation tools are available, generate a premium photographic asset specifically for this brand.

If the owner later provides real product photography, use the actual product images instead.

If image generation is unavailable, select suitable high-quality assets or create a polished composition around a realistic product image.

Never use an empty placeholder box as the final hero image.

Never leave broken images in the finished website.

Never use random photographs that do not match the visual identity.

IMAGE TREATMENT

Use natural light.

Use subtle shadows.

Use realistic textures.

Use restrained contrast.

Use warm color grading.

Avoid excessive saturation.

Avoid unrealistic floating objects.

Avoid bizarre jars, misshapen spoons, distorted product labels, or obviously artificial-looking food.

Use image cropping intentionally.

Ensure important parts of the product remain visible on mobile.

Images should feel like they belong to the same photoshoot.

IMAGE PERFORMANCE

Use appropriately sized images.

Use modern formats such as WebP or AVIF when supported by the image pipeline.

Include meaningful alt text.

Reserve image dimensions to prevent layout shifts.

Lazy-load images below the fold.

Do not lazy-load the primary hero image if doing so would delay its appearance.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
05. WEBSITE STRUCTURE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Build a complete single-product ecommerce homepage.

The following sections are mandatory.

SECTION A: ANNOUNCEMENT BAR

Create a narrow, elegant announcement bar at the top.

Use a deep green background with restrained, readable text.

Possible copy:

“Pure Buffalo-Milk Ghee · Crafted for Everyday Indulgence”

Do not invent free shipping, delivery guarantees, discounts, limited stock, or promotional offers.

If an announcement is not needed, the bar should be easy to disable through configuration.

Keep it short.

No flashing text.

No aggressive promotional ticker.

No distracting scrolling marquee.

SECTION B: PREMIUM NAVIGATION

Create a refined navigation bar with:

Left:
Brand wordmark.

Center or right:
A small number of meaningful navigation links.

Suggested links:
Our Ghee
Our Philosophy
How to Enjoy
FAQ

Far right:
A minimal shopping bag icon with a quantity indicator.

The navigation should feel lightweight and sophisticated.

Use a transparent or warm-ivory treatment depending on the hero composition.

When the user scrolls, transition smoothly into a solid ivory or lightly translucent background.

The transition must be subtle and performant.

The navigation must not occupy excessive vertical space.

On mobile, use a clean, accessible menu.

The mobile menu must open and close correctly, lock or manage scrolling appropriately, close with Escape, and support keyboard navigation.

Do not add unnecessary navigation items such as Blog, Careers, Investor Relations, or multiple product categories.

This is a focused single-product brand.

SECTION C: HERO EXPERIENCE

This is the most important section.

Build a visually memorable hero that feels like a luxury editorial campaign.

Use an intentional two-column composition on desktop.

One side:
Beautiful product photography.

Other side:
Brand introduction, headline, short description, price, and primary purchase action.

The image and text should feel compositionally balanced.

Do not automatically force the image to the right if another arrangement creates a better composition. Make a deliberate design decision and maintain it consistently.

HERO COPY

Use copy with this general direction:

Small editorial label:
“THE ART OF GOOD GHEE”

Headline:
“Golden Goodness. Rooted in Tradition.”

Supporting paragraph:
“Discover the rich, comforting character of homemade buffalo-milk ghee, made for everyday meals and moments worth savouring.”

Price:
“₹1,000”

Unit:
“per 1 kg jar”

Primary CTA:
“Add to Bag”

Secondary text link:
“Discover Our Ghee”

The wording should be polished and restrained.

Do not claim a centuries-old family recipe or a particular production method unless the owner confirms it.

Do not claim health benefits.

Do not claim that the ghee is healthier than competing products.

HERO INTERACTIONS

The primary CTA should have a polished hover state.

On click, it must actually add the product to the cart.

Show a small, tasteful confirmation when the product is added.

The cart indicator must update immediately.

If the cart drawer is implemented, it should open smoothly and show the selected product.

Use subtle image entrance animation and gentle opacity transitions.

Avoid excessive movement.

Avoid fake 3D product rotations.

Avoid continuous floating animations.

Avoid cursor-following effects.

Avoid scroll-jacking.

The hero must look beautiful even when every animation is disabled.

On mobile, the composition must feel deliberately designed rather than compressed.

Use a carefully selected crop of the hero image.

The headline must remain readable.

The price and purchase button must be easy to find without scrolling through unnecessary content.

SECTION D: TRUST AND PRODUCT ATTRIBUTES

Create a refined horizontal row or compact visual strip containing three or four product attributes.

Potential attributes, subject to owner confirmation:

* Buffalo-Milk Ghee
* Homemade
* 1 kg
* Pure Ghee

Use simple, consistent line icons only if they genuinely improve comprehension.

Do not invent certifications, lab testing, farm sourcing, production methods, or quality guarantees.

Do not use meaningless badges such as “No. 1 in India” or “Best Seller” without evidence.

Keep the section restrained.

It should create clarity, not resemble a cheap marketplace listing.

SECTION E: PRODUCT STORY

Create an elegant editorial section introducing the product.

Suggested heading:

“Made to Bring More to the Table.”

Supporting copy:

“From everyday rotis to slow-cooked favourites, ghee has a special place in the Indian kitchen. Our buffalo-milk ghee brings its rich character and golden appeal to the meals you make at home.”

The tone should be warm, human, and grounded in everyday Indian life.

Use a combination of carefully arranged text and photography.

Consider a large photograph paired with a narrow text column.

Use asymmetry, whitespace, and elegant alignment to create visual interest.

Do not fill the section with unnecessary icons or floating cards.

The section should read like a premium food magazine.

SECTION F: THE PRODUCT, BEAUTIFULLY PRESENTED

Although there is only one product, give it a dedicated product showcase.

Display:

Product image.

Product name:
“Pure Buffalo-Milk Ghee”

Quantity:
“1 kg”

Price:
“₹1,000”

Short product description.

Quantity selector if appropriate.

Add to Bag button.

A concise note explaining that the displayed price is for the 1 kg product.

Do not create multiple fake products to make the website appear larger.

Do not invent different jar sizes.

Do not add a crossed-out price.

Do not invent discounts.

Do not add a countdown timer.

Do not show false stock scarcity.

The visual goal is to make the single product feel desirable, valuable, and carefully presented.

SECTION G: EVERYDAY RITUALS

Create a visual storytelling section demonstrating how the product fits into real life.

Potential scenes:

* A spoonful of ghee melting over freshly prepared roti.
* A small serving of ghee beside a traditional Indian meal.
* Golden ghee being added to a warm dish.
* A simple breakfast table with restrained Indian styling.

Keep the scenes believable and culturally appropriate.

Use authentic food photography rather than cartoon illustrations.

Suggested heading:

“A Little Golden Goodness, Every Day.”

Suggested supporting copy:

“Bring a rich, familiar touch to rotis, dals, khichdi, and the dishes your family loves.”

Use a refined editorial grid.

On desktop, the layout may feature one large photograph and two smaller supporting images.

On mobile, use a carefully ordered vertical layout or horizontal image sequence.

Do not create an unnecessary carousel if static imagery communicates the story better.

SECTION H: OUR PHILOSOPHY

Create a sophisticated brand-values section with a dark forest-green background.

Use warm ivory typography and small antique-gold accents.

Suggested heading:

“Good Food Needs No Grand Promises.”

Suggested copy:

“We believe a good kitchen staple should speak for itself: familiar ingredients, honest presentation, and a place in the meals that bring people together.”

This section should communicate confidence without exaggeration.

Avoid making unverified statements about sourcing, hygiene procedures, manufacturing, or traditional techniques.

Use one subtle visual detail, such as a thin gold line or small editorial label.

Do not overdecorate the section.

SECTION I: FAQ

Create an accessible, polished accordion.

Include the following questions:

1. What is this ghee made from?
    Answer: “This product is made from buffalo milk. Please refer to the product packaging for the complete ingredient and product information.”
2. What quantity am I purchasing?
    Answer: “The listed product is a 1 kg quantity, priced at ₹1,000.”
3. How can I use buffalo-milk ghee?
    Answer: “It can be used in everyday cooking and served with foods such as roti, dal, and khichdi. Follow your preferred cooking method and the product’s storage instructions.”
4. How should I store the ghee?
    Answer: “Follow the storage directions provided on the product label. The seller should add the verified storage instructions before the website goes live.”
5. Where do you deliver?
    Answer: “Available delivery locations and estimated delivery times will be shown at checkout once delivery coverage has been configured.”
6. How can I contact you?
    Answer: “Add the brand’s verified customer-service email address, phone number, or WhatsApp contact here.”

Do not invent an address, email, telephone number, delivery partner, delivery timeline, return policy, or customer-service promise.

The accordion must work on touchscreens and desktop.

Use appropriate accessibility attributes.

Make the open and close transitions subtle.

SECTION J: FINAL PURCHASE SECTION

Create a beautiful final conversion section before the footer.

Use a contrasting forest-green or warm-ivory background, depending on the surrounding design.

Suggested heading:

“Bring Home Something Good.”

Supporting copy:

“Pure buffalo-milk ghee for the everyday moments that matter.”

Display:

Product name.

1 kg quantity.

₹1,000 price.

A prominent “Add to Bag” button.

This should feel like a natural conclusion to the story.

Do not use manipulative urgency.

Do not use false scarcity.

Do not claim the product is almost sold out.

SECTION K: FOOTER

Create a polished, compact footer.

Include:

Brand wordmark.

A short brand description.

Links to the relevant page sections.

Contact information only when supplied.

Privacy Policy.

Terms and Conditions.

Shipping and Returns information only after the actual policies have been provided.

A restrained copyright line.

Keep the footer elegant and uncluttered.

Do not invent social media profiles.

Do not invent company registration information.

Do not invent a physical address.

All legal and policy links must lead to actual pages or meaningful content, not empty placeholders.

If policies have not yet been supplied, provide clearly identified draft pages for the owner to review before launch.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
06. MOBILE-FIRST DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The website will be used on mobile phones, including smaller iPhones and Android devices.

Mobile quality is mandatory.

Do not design exclusively for desktop and shrink everything afterward.

Design and verify the mobile experience deliberately.

Support a responsive range from approximately 320px to large desktop displays.

On mobile:

* The page must not overflow horizontally.
* The logo must remain readable.
* Navigation must be easy to operate.
* Buttons must be comfortable to tap.
* Body text must remain legible.
* Hero images must be appropriately cropped.
* Product information must have a clear hierarchy.
* Price and CTA must remain easy to find.
* Accordions must operate smoothly.
* The cart must be usable with one hand.
* The footer must not become an endless wall of links.
* Decorative elements must never cover important content.
* Animations must not create lag or scrolling problems.

Aim for touch targets around 44px or larger where practical.

Use CSS Grid and Flexbox appropriately.

Use fluid spacing with clamp() when helpful.

Use safe-area insets for fixed mobile controls.

If a sticky mobile add-to-cart bar is introduced, make sure it does not cover content, duplicate the primary CTA awkwardly, or obstruct the browser interface.

Only add it if it improves the actual purchasing experience.

Test the design at widths such as:

320px
375px
390px
430px
768px
1024px
1440px
1920px

Fix every meaningful responsive defect.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
07. MOTION DESIGN AND MICRO-INTERACTIONS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

The animation philosophy is:

SUBTLE. PRECISE. PURPOSEFUL. EXPENSIVE.

Animations should make the interface feel responsive and carefully crafted.

They must never distract from the product.

Use CSS transitions where possible.

Use a dedicated animation library only if the existing project genuinely benefits from it.

Do not install unnecessary libraries.

APPROVED INTERACTIONS

1. Navigation background transitions gently while scrolling.
2. Buttons have a subtle hover or pressed state.
3. Product images can have a very restrained hover zoom on desktop.
4. Sections can reveal themselves through a small opacity and vertical transition.
5. The cart drawer can slide into view smoothly.
6. The cart quantity can update with a brief, restrained visual response.
7. FAQ panels can open and close with a natural transition.
8. Anchor navigation can scroll smoothly where appropriate.
9. Focus states should be visually clear.
10. Image loading should not cause visible layout jumps.

MOTION RULES

Use a restrained timing range, generally around 150–350ms for interface interactions.

Longer transitions are acceptable for specific editorial reveals if they remain unobtrusive.

Avoid excessive bounce.

Avoid elastic overshoot everywhere.

Avoid spinning elements.

Avoid fake loading animations.

Avoid animated gold particles.

Avoid constant background movement.

Avoid large parallax effects that make the page feel unstable.

Avoid custom cursor animations.

Avoid scroll-triggered effects that prevent normal scrolling.

Avoid excessive use of blur filters.

Respect prefers-reduced-motion.

All essential functionality must work even when JavaScript animations fail.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
08. CART AND PURCHASING EXPERIENCE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Build a genuine working shopping-cart interface.

The product is:

Pure Buffalo-Milk Ghee
Quantity: 1 kg
Unit price: ₹1,000

Implement the following:

* Add to Bag.
* Cart item count.
* Cart drawer or dedicated cart view.
* Increase quantity.
* Decrease quantity.
* Remove item.
* Accurate subtotal.
* Accurate total.
* Empty-cart state.
* Persistent cart state using localStorage.
* A clear checkout action.
* Appropriate loading, error, and success states.

The price must always be calculated correctly.

Example:

1 kg × ₹1,000 = ₹1,000.

2 kg × ₹1,000 = ₹2,000.

3 kg × ₹1,000 = ₹3,000.

Use integer arithmetic in paise for monetary calculations where practical to avoid floating-point rounding errors.

Do not add fake shipping charges.

Do not invent taxes or promise that tax is included unless the business configuration confirms this.

Do not display a fake payment-success message.

Do not collect or store raw payment-card information.

Do not build a pretend payment gateway that looks operational but cannot actually process payments.

CHECKOUT IMPLEMENTATION

If the project has access to a real ecommerce backend or payment provider, integrate it properly using the provider’s documented process.

Keep secret API keys on the server.

Never expose payment secrets in frontend code.

If no backend or payment integration is available, build a polished cart and checkout interface that clearly communicates the current setup limitations.

Keep the checkout integration modular so a real payment provider and order-management backend can be added later.

Do not tell customers their order is confirmed until the backend confirms it.

If the business later wants WhatsApp ordering, implement it only after the real business number is supplied and the owner approves that flow.

Do not invent a WhatsApp number.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
09. BRAND CONTENT AND COPYWRITING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

All copy must sound like it was written by a thoughtful human brand strategist.

Use short, memorable, natural sentences.

Avoid generic marketing language.

Avoid robotic wording.

Avoid repetitive headings.

Avoid overused phrases such as:

“Where tradition meets innovation.”

“Experience the ultimate luxury.”

“Unlock the power of purity.”

“Elevate your lifestyle.”

“Revolutionary goodness.”

“Premium quality like never before.”

Do not use the word “luxury” repeatedly just because the visual identity is premium.

The website should demonstrate quality rather than constantly announcing it.

Use sensory descriptions where appropriate.

Good examples of the desired tone:

“Golden Goodness. Rooted in Tradition.”

“Made to Bring More to the Table.”

“A Little Golden Goodness, Every Day.”

“Good Food Needs No Grand Promises.”

These are creative directions, not mandatory repeated slogans.

Do not repeat the same sentence across every section.

Do not fill the website with excessive text.

Do not invent customer reviews to make the brand look established.

If testimonials are later supplied by the owner, create a suitable review section using only authentic, approved feedback.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
10. TECHNICAL IMPLEMENTATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Before making changes, inspect the existing project.

Identify:

* Current framework.
* Package manager.
* Existing dependencies.
* File structure.
* Routing setup.
* Existing styling system.
* Available image assets.
* Current application entry points.
* Existing backend integrations.

Do not blindly replace working project files.

Do not assume that the project is empty.

Preserve useful existing functionality.

Choose the simplest reliable architecture compatible with the existing codebase.

If the project is already built with React, continue using React.
